description: Somos Alcubierre, un equipo multidisciplinario de mentes audaces e ingenieros de frontera. Fusionamos computación cuántica aplicada, agentes de IA , modelos matemáticos avanzados, para redefinir los límites de la exploración espacial y la colonización planetaria.. Diseñamos un sistema táctico de navegación que integra datos científicos complejos para mapear rutas críticas (Marswalks),
summary:
It is a 100% Offline-First Augmented Reality Heads-Up Display (HUD) and hyper-localized tactical dashboard designed for autonomous exploration in extreme environments lacking satellite coverage or a stable magnetic field (such as the Martian surface or deep underground mining galleries).
(Tactical Interface & Autonomous Navigation Subsystem — Operation Tharsis–Alcubierre | MarsSigma Research Seedbed, ITM Medellín)
The system integrates six scientific layers of NASA orbital and environmental data (MOLA, HiRISE, CRISM, THEMIS, MEDA, and RAD) alongside a quantized local Artificial Intelligence engine (Edge AI — Phi-3) running directly on the explorer's hardware. This enables a priori safe route calculation, identification of reusable resources (ISRU and metallic scrap), and manual optical geodetic triangulation (Fail-Safe) using the Tharsis volcanoes (Arsia Mons, Pavonis Mons, and Ascraeus Mons) as reference landmarks when inertial sensors drift.
details:
Project Overview: ARES RESILIENCE (Operation Tharsis–Alcubierre) ARES RESILIENCE is a 100% Offline-First Augmented Reality Heads-Up Display (HUD) and hyper-localized tactical navigation interface developed by the MarsSigma Research Seedbed (Instituto Tecnológico Metropolitano — ITM Medellín, Colombia). Designed for human explorers and autonomous rovers operating in extreme environments devoid of satellite constellations (GPS) or stable global magnetic fields—such as the Martian Tharsis volcanic province or deep underground mining galleries—the system ensures sovereign navigation, resource recovery, and crew survival.

How It Works

  1. Hyper-Localized Multilayer Base Map: Prior to deployment, the system ingests and fuses six orbital and surface NASA datasets (MOLA, HiRISE, CRISM, THEMIS, MEDA, and RAD) into a local Digital Elevation Model (DEM) centered on Arsia Mons ("Punto Cero"). Because Mars lacks a global dipole magnetic field and exhibits localized crustal magnetic anomalies that render conventional compasses useless, this preloaded topographic database acts as an "intellectual compass."
  2. Edge AI A Priori Decision Engine: Running quantized local language models (Phi-3, 4-bit quantization via Ollama/Llama.cpp) directly on low-power edge hardware without cloud or Earth-link latency, the system continuously cross-references inertial odometry (IMU) and 3D LiDAR/stereo vision against the preloaded scientific layers. In under 50 milliseconds, it computes safe a priori traversal routes avoiding slopes $>15^\circ$ and boulders $>0.5\text{ m}$, triggers automatic shelter diversions toward subsurface lava tubes (Arsia N-3) during Solar Particle Events (SPE), and identifies In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) targets—including shallow water ice, perchlorates, and recoverable metallic scrap (such as Ti-6Al-4V alloys from descent stages) for autonomous additive manufacturing at Kiosko Infinity ($\pm 0.5\text{ mm}$ tolerance).
  3. Fail-Safe Optical Geodetic Calibration: To eliminate accumulated IMU drift when orbital relays fail, the astronaut uses the helmet HUD reticle as an optical theodolite. By sighting two or more prominent volcanic peaks on the horizon (Arsia Mons, Pavonis Mons, and Ascraeus Mons), an embedded non-linear least-squares solver (3D Gauss-Newton / Spherical Snellius-Pothenot resection) calculates the explorer's exact $(X,Y,Z)$ coordinates on the MOLA ellipsoid in real time.
  4. Benefits, Intended Impact & Dual-Use Transfer
  • Space Exploration: Eliminates dependency on the 4-to-22-minute Earth communication delay, ensuring crew autonomy and cognitive ergonomics during Extravehicular Activities (EVAs).
  • Terrestrial Dual-Use (Colombian Underground Mining): The exact same offline sensor bus (3D LiDAR + IMU + gas telemetry) and HUD interface transfer directly to deep underground mining operations in Colombia, preventing disorientation and saving lives in GPS-denied, hazardous subterranean tunnels.

Tools, Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Software & Languages: Python (alcubierre_master.py for Gauss-Newton geodetic resection and stochastic route optimization), HTML5/CSS3/JavaScript & Three.js/WebGL (index.html for the interactive 3D tactical HUD and digital twin), NumPy, SciPy.
  • Edge AI Runtime: Quantized Microsoft Phi-3 (4-bit) running locally via Ollama / Llama.cpp on ARM/mobile GPU edge nodes.
  • Quality & Metrology Framework: Statistical tolerance control ($\pm 0.5\text{ mm}$) and cognitive ergonomics modeling developed under ITM Quality Engineering methodologies.

Creativity & Design Considerations Instead of treating lack of connectivity and magnetic interference as mission-stopping limitations, our team turned Martian geography itself into a navigation instrument (using the Tharsis Montes as natural geodetic monuments) and reframed mission debris into industrial feedstock. Every visual asset and telemetry layer in the HUD was optimized for high-contrast peripheral readability (Obsidian Black, Emerald Green, Orbital Cyan) and ultra-lightweight web deployment under an Open Science framework.
